title: Event
description: The base envelope every L.I.O.N.E.L event carries. TurnEvent, WorkflowEvent, AuditRecord and Metrics all specialize it. Defining the envelope once is what lets a single OpenTelemetry trace stitch across both planes and both runtimes (ADR-0006, ADR-0019) — if each subsystem invented its own correlation field, that stitching would be impossible.

compatibility.notes: This is the most-consumed contract in the system, so it is the most expensive to change — which is the point of recording four consumers. Adding a REQUIRED field here breaks every producer at once. Adding an optional one is safe. `event_id` and `emitted_at` are deliberately the only universally required fields beyond `kind`: everything else varies by specialization, and forcing more into the base would push subsystem concerns into shared ground.

kind.description: Discriminator selecting the specialization. Consumers MUST skip unknown kinds rather than failing — a dashboard that cannot render a new event kind is acceptable; one that crashes is not.

turn_id.description: ALSO THE OPENTELEMETRY TRACE ID. Absent only for events outside any turn (process lifecycle, scheduled jobs).

seq.description: Monotonic within a turn. A gap means events were dropped.

attributes.description: Reserved names in events/v1/telemetry-attributes.schema.json. MUST NOT carry secrets, raw transcripts, or file contents.

Ulid.description: 26-char Crockford base32 (excludes I, L, O, U to avoid visual ambiguity with 1 and 0). Chosen over UUIDv4 because ULIDs sort lexicographically by creation time, which makes log and trace listings chronological for free.

Tier.description: ADR-0007. Recorded per event because the latency budget differs per tier and a cross-tier comparison is meaningless.

Component.description: Closed set so dashboards can group reliably. Adding a component is a MINOR change; consumers treat unknown values as 'other'.
